title: ARTEX closes its source after an AI security agent is linked to bank attacks
friendlyTitle: An AI security tool goes closed-source after bank attacks
summary: The developer of ARTEX has stopped public releases and converted the penetration-testing agent to closed source after CrowdStrike linked it to attacks targeting South Korean banks. Reuters reports that ARTEX connected to external models such as Claude, ChatGPT and DeepSeek to automate security testing; at least nine banks have disclosed or reportedly experienced attacks since late September.
friendlySummary: ARTEX was made to automate security testing, but investigators say it was used in attacks on South Korean banks. Its developer has stopped public updates and closed the source code.
whyItMatters: Dual-use agent frameworks can turn a model’s capabilities into repeatable actions against real systems. Security teams should not treat an open-source label or defensive purpose as a control: powerful tools still need authorised targets, isolated environments, identity limits, monitoring and a rapid way to revoke access.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A useful security tool can also be misused. Organisations should limit where agents can connect, watch what they do and be ready to remove access quickly.
